subject.title: Improve doctor/gateway diagnostics clarity for mixed LaunchAgent/runtime states

question: Should `openclaw doctor` grow a composed final gateway diagnosis model that combines RPC health, LaunchAgent/service runtime, service-config drift, port/client clues, and channel conflict hints, and should that model expose a machine-readable diagnosis block?
rationale: Current main already collects most underlying facts, but the verdict states, cause precedence, action ordering, and JSON shape are stable CLI/operator UX decisions that automation should not invent.

options.title: Add composed doctor verdict
options.body: Render one final healthy/degraded/down-style diagnosis with probable causes and ordered recovery steps while reusing existing doctor, gateway, service, and channel facts.

options.title: Reuse status-all diagnosis first
options.body: Promote the existing `status --all` diagnosis model into a shared read-only helper before changing doctor output.

options.title: Only tune individual panels
options.body: Keep the current independent doctor panels and improve strings only after a live mixed-state transcript narrows the confusing output.

recommendation.title: Add composed doctor verdict
recommendation.body: Render one final healthy/degraded/down-style diagnosis with probable causes and ordered recovery steps while reusing existing doctor, gateway, service, and channel facts.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses doctor, gateway probe, service-runtime, and operator diagnosis surfaces where steipete has the strongest recent product/history signal.
